title: Makes someone a good friend
keyIdea: A good friend is kind, honest, fair and someone you can count on: they keep promises and let others join in. Being bossy, saying mean things and leaving people out are not friendly. All friends fall out sometimes. You can make up: calm down, say sorry, then play again.

kid: A good friend is kind. They say nice things and help you. A good friend lets you join in the game.
A good friend is fair. If you want different games, you take turns to choose. Bossy means you always get your way. That is not fair.
A good friend tells the truth, even after a mistake. They keep their promises. If they say they will save you a seat, they do.
Friends fall out sometimes. That is OK. Take a big breath. Say sorry. Then play again. You can still be friends.
adult: This topic is the 'Caring friendships' strand of the DfE guidance for Relationships Education (2019). Pupils learn what good friendships are like: respect, truth, trust, loyalty, kindness and sharing. They also learn that most friendships have ups and downs, and that these can often be worked through. The PSHE Association Key Stage 1 programme and the IB PYP strand on interactions set the same goals for ages 5 to 7.

At this age a friend is often whoever a child is playing with right now. So the lesson names the qualities that make a friendship last. These are kindness, honesty, keeping promises (being reliable), fairness (taking turns to choose) and letting others join (inclusion). It also names unfriendly acts a child can spot: being bossy, unkind words and leaving people out.

Common mistakes: thinking one falling out ends a friendship for good; treating friendship as a deal, as in 'you can play if you give me your car'; thinking a good friend always agrees with you; and fibbing to dodge trouble after an accident. Be careful not to call a child a bad friend. Talk about what they did, and show how to repair it: calm down, say sorry, then play again.

In the lab your child pins good-friend badges on a friend. They choose fair and kind moves when games clash or someone asks to join. They own up and keep a promise, put the steps of making up in order, and spot the unfriendly picture in a strip.

familyTip: Over tea, ask: "Who was a good friend to you today? What did they do?" Then ask: "When were you a good friend?" Name the quality, such as kind, honest or fair.

visual.caption: Good friend or not friendly? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: pin good-friend badges, choose fair and honest moves, put the steps of making up in order, and spot unfriendly behaviour.

practice.prompt: You want to play blocks. Your friend wants to play tag. What does a good friend do?
choices: Take turns: tag first, then blocks
Shout until they play blocks
Go off and play alone in a huff
practice.hint: A good friend is fair. How can you both get a go?
practice.explain: Taking turns to choose is fair, so you both get to play your game. Shouting to get your way is bossy.

practice.prompt: {a} children are playing a game. {b} more children ask to join, and the group says yes. How many children are playing now?
practice.hint: Good friends let others join. Add the new children to the group.
practice.explain: {a} children and {b} more who joined makes {=a+b} children playing together.

practice.prompt: You broke your friend's crayon by mistake. What does a good friend do?
choices: Tell them and say sorry
Hide it and say nothing
Say someone else did it
practice.hint: A good friend is honest, even after a mistake.
practice.explain: Telling the truth and saying sorry is honest. Your friend can trust you, and you can sort it out together.

practice.prompt: You and your friend take turns to choose the game. There are {n} turns at playtime. How many turns do you get to choose?
practice.hint: Turns go me, you, me, you. Split the turns into two fair groups.
practice.explain: {n} turns shared fairly between two friends is {=n/2} turns each.

pool.prompt: Which one is being a good friend?
choices: Ella, who lets new children join
Max, who says: do what I say!
Jo, who only plays if you give her sweets
pool.hint: Look for kind, fair and letting others join.
pool.explain: Ella lets others join, which is kind. Max is bossy, and a friend should not make you pay to play like Jo.

pool.prompt: You and your friend had a big fall-out. Can you still be friends?
choices: Yes, you can make up
No, never again
Only if they say sorry first
pool.hint: All friends fall out sometimes. What can you do to fix it?
pool.explain: Friends have ups and downs. Calm down, say sorry and play again. You do not have to wait for them to go first.

pool.prompt: You said you would play with Sam at break. Then Ben asks you to play. What does a good friend do?
choices: Keep the promise and play with Sam
Go with Ben and say nothing
Hide from both of them
pool.hint: You made a promise. What does a friend you can count on do?
pool.explain: Keeping your promise means Sam can trust you. You could ask Ben to join you both.

pool.prompt: A friend has {n} stickers and shares {k} with you. How many does your friend have left?
pool.hint: Start with {n} stickers and take away the {k} your friend gave you.
pool.explain: {n} take away {k} is {=n-k}, so your friend has {=n-k} stickers left after sharing.

pool.prompt: A boy whispers and points at a girl, then laughs. Is he being a good friend?
choices: No, that is mean
Yes, it is only a joke
Yes, if his friends laugh too
pool.hint: Think about how the girl feels when someone points and laughs at her.
pool.explain: Whispering, pointing and laughing at someone is mean. It makes her feel sad and left out.

pool.prompt: Kim calls you a mean name, then says sorry. What could you do?
choices: Say thank you for saying sorry, and play again
Call her a mean name back
Tell everyone not to play with her
pool.hint: She said sorry. How do friends make up?
pool.explain: Saying sorry is how friends fix a fall-out. Accepting it lets you play again. Being mean back keeps the fall-out going.

pool.prompt: Which word means a friend who keeps their promises?
choices: Someone you can count on
Bossy
Sneaky
pool.hint: If they say they will do it, do they do it?
pool.explain: A friend you can count on does what they said. Bossy means always telling others what to do.

pool.prompt: {a} friends are playing tag. {b} of them have to go home. How many are still playing?
pool.hint: Start with {a} friends and take away the {b} who went home.
pool.explain: {a} take away {b} is {=a-b}, so {=a-b} friends are still playing tag.
